question: Do direct, fixed byte encodings of LP2 rune indices or GP primes form whole-stream ordinary text or a recognizable file beginning?
targets: Each nonempty LP2-00–55 page separately, plus those pages concatenated in order; use rune order from pinned text records and omit only visible spacing and punctuation.
encodings: index-5-msb: each zero-based GP index as five high-bit-first bits; append zero bits to byte boundary at the end of each target
index-5-lsb: reverse the five bits within each index token, then group high-bit-first into bytes; append zero bits at end
prime-byte: each GP prime value as one unsigned byte, without truncation
acceptance: Require every byte to be printable ASCII, tab, LF or CR; separately require strict UTF-8 validity; separately match PNG, gzip, ZIP, PDF, ELF or MZ at offset zero. Header matches are candidates, never proof of a valid file. UTF-8 validity alone is not evidence of readable text.
controls: Known synthetic ASCII and all six file-prefix examples must trigger their corresponding screens; independent checker derives rune streams from page JSON and rebuilds byte arrays.
exclusions: Per-word prime sums, alternate widths and endianness, arithmetic changes, compression, headers away from offset zero, choice of page/order based on output, language scoring and executable behavior. No generated bytes are run as code.
